frames.observation: The exact custom tentacle is readable in settled native Tentacle_Idle_M. Its thick dark teal and green body, orange bands, green streaks and base fins form one coherent low-poly silhouette; the tall upper section continues beyond the camera frame.

A later Tentacle_Idle_M sample preserves the same planted base, body width, surface pattern and attached fins while the body leans through its idle motion. The upper body remains outside this camera crop.

During native Tentacle_Attack2_M, the custom body bends diagonally toward the hero and remains continuous across its orange band and surface pattern. A bright native effect obscures the contact area, and the upper section is clipped by the camera.

The late Tentacle_Attack2_M pose carries the same custom body upright over the hero with its main segments still connected. Native effects, foreground overlap and the camera crop prevent inspection of the full tip; the visible 10-damage label belongs to the native enemy attack against the hero.
The ordinary zero-focus player attack begins with Sargassum Lash V2 intact at HP162 in settled Tentacle_Idle_M. The planted lower body and visible surface details match the earlier idle capture.
A second pre-impact idle sample preserves the same connected lower silhouette and HP162 state. This frame precedes the measured HP transition and does not establish hit motion by itself.

The telemetry-selected native Damaged trigger coincides with a bright impact sphere and foreground hero. The lower custom body remains aligned behind them, while the visible HP156 is an intermediate UI state and does not alone establish the final 8-damage result.

At HP154 in native Tentacle_Damaged_M, the tentacle bends into its recoil while the body, orange band, green streaks and base fins remain connected. The camera still excludes the top of this unusually tall model.

Native Tentacle_AttackGrab_Mirrored curls the large custom body into a broad loop across the foreground. The visible bands, patterned segments and terminal form remain coherent, but the close motion covers the hero and prevents a complete silhouette judgment in this frame.

The capture ends during native Tentacle_Attack1_M with the custom tentacle arcing over the hero. Its thick body and surface details remain continuous through the sampled pose, while native impact effects and the foreground crop limit fine inspection.

The explicit KillSingle capture begins with the exact custom tentacle intact at HP154 in native Tentacle_Idle_M. Attack-selection UI overlaps the scene; this action is a separate death fixture rather than ordinary lethal gameplay.

At the telemetry-selected native Death trigger, the custom tentacle remains upright at the left edge while a large native impact sphere covers the central action. The effect prevents a detailed whole-body judgment at this instant.

Native Tentacle_Death has begun and the custom body is retracting toward the rear of the combat space. The visible vertical segment preserves its teal and green surface and orange band, with no native mesh substitution visible.

The animated withdrawal has moved the custom tentacle outside the rendered camera view while exact telemetry still reports the renderer active, enabled, visible and playing Tentacle_Death. This image proves absence from this camera view only.
The combat space remains clear while Tentacle_Death continues on the exact active renderer outside the camera view. This does not establish a corpse state, collision, cleanup cause or final disposal.

At the final retained frame before controller teardown, no tentacle pixels are visible and telemetry still preserves the exact active, enabled, reported-visible renderer identity in Tentacle_Death. The view does not reveal what is outside the camera.

The final retained boundary frame shows the Ready handoff with no target pixels. Telemetry records the same renderer disabled at its owner, not visible, and the animator disabled; the next requested sample reports renderer destruction, so later death duration and cleanup causality remain unproven.

requirements: All 17 referenced original PNGs were inspected before assigning the reviewed status.
Every observation is scoped to the exact frame and its telemetry boundary.

The ordinary zero-focus native hammer hit reduced the target from 162 to 154 HP with recorded damage 8 and a Damaged response. It is separate from the explicit KillSingle fixture, which reduced 154 to 0 with recorded damage 1000 and a Death response.

The source reports m_DoRagdoll false with zero rigidbodies. Death is animator-driven: Tentacle_Death is observed from frames 30 through 89, followed by an inactive, not-visible renderer and disabled animator at retained frame 90.

Exact renderer instance, owner, CEL, mesh and bone signature remain unchanged through all 331 retained telemetry frames. The renderer is active and reported visible in 330 frames and enabled in all 331; the accepted 91-frame death prefix ends because the renderer is destroyed before the next requested sample.
The disposable party maximum-HP fixture protects the hero but does not alter enemy actions or establish representative balance. The native pass action reduced hero HP from 999 to 989.
Strict Ready is observed at dungeon level 0, room 2, with one active Ready button. No Collect action was taken, and this review makes no Collect claim.

The tall tentacle extends beyond the fixed camera in several idle and attack samples. These captures establish the sampled poses and exact binding, not all-angle culling, full-tip appearance, collision, corpse lifetime, cleanup causality, final disposal or finished-art acceptance.
